headline: Brent handed back $4 of its Houthi premium while WTI pushed to $101 and copper/gold printed a 52-week high — the commodity tape stopped confirming the growth scare that MOVE at z=1.93 still insists on.
summary: What changed overnight is the oil tape. Brent fell 2.5% to 110.30 after tagging a five-month high on the Saudi/Libya supply scare, while WTI rose 1.8% to 101.27 — the grade gap collapsed from roughly $13.9 to $9.03 in one session. That is the risk premium draining out of seaborne barrels, not demand accelerating. RBOB fell another 1.6% and is -12.8% on the month at z=-1.27, the pump disinflation that makes the CPI index (z=0.65, +106bp ytd) survivable. Copper added 1.8% to 6.477 and copper/gold rose 2.3% to the 99th percentile of its year, with nat gas +11.4%. Asia stopped bleeding: Hang Seng +0.7%, Shanghai +0.9%, KOSPI +0.3% after a -21.6% month, with CNY at 6.6596, its strongest print in a year.

But nothing in the vol complex relented. VIX is +4.0% at 19.79 (z=1.17, acceleration 0.88), VIX3M +8.8% on the week, and VIX/VIX3M at 0.946 with z=1.95 and acceleration 1.30 — both ends of the curve are now lifting, so yesterday's advice to roll hedges out is already half-priced. SKEW 152.39. MOVE sits at 106.84, +36% on the month, z=1.93, 39.7% above its 200-day — bond vol exploding into a 17bp belly rally is a flight, not a policy repricing. The inflation twist got worse, not better: 5-year breakevens 2.45% (+13bp on the month, z=0.56) against 10-year breakevens 2.32% (-1bp). Near-term prices up, long-term growth down. The 30-year mortgage is still 7.32%, +37bp on the month, 94th percentile. Risk regime unchanged at -24; rates -56, inflation -45.

The internals still say AI unwind, not market de-risking, and that distinction is where the money is. SOXX is -17.0% on the month (z=-1.99, acceleration -1.93), MU -21.9%, AMD -18.6%, EWY -22.6%, KOSPI 1-month z=-3.0 — a semiconductor capital-cycle de-rating being exported through Korea and Taiwan. Against that, RSP/SPY is +3.8% on the month with acceleration z=3.01, XLP, XLV, IWD and USMV all sit at the 100th percentile of their year, and SPHB/SPLV has fallen 15.9% in a month to z=-2.52. The cleanest expression of the rotation is inside tech, not out of it: IGV/SMH +18.2% on the month, z=2.63, acceleration 2.12, with CIBR +17.2% over three months.

The accidents are localized and worth respecting. USDMXN at 18.779 is the single most stretched series on the board — z=3.14, 100th percentile, +8.6% on the month, acceleration 1.54 — while the local IPC is +8.4% on the month; equity up, currency down is a debasement tape, not a bull market. The AI-power complex keeps imploding even with gas +11.4%: NLR -18.9%, URA -22.1%, REMX -27.3%, GRID -10.6% on the month, GEV -12.9%, ETN at z=-2.45. Credit is lagging quietly rather than breaking: HYG/IEF -1.9% on the month at z=-1.49 with acceleration -1.06, HYG at the 37th percentile, BKLN z=-1.10. And the precious liquidation rolls on — gold 4039 at the 6th percentile, silver -16.1% on the month, GDXJ -20.9%, gold/silver +11.5% with acceleration 1.44.

good.text: Copper +1.8% to 6.477 and copper/gold +2.3% to the 99th percentile — the industrial metal is refusing to ratify the equity growth scare.

Brent -2.5% to 110.30 against WTI +1.8% to 101.27 narrows the grade gap to ~$9.0, and gasoline is -12.8% on the month (z=-1.27): the geopolitical tax on the consumer is shrinking even with crude over $100.
The median stock is fine: RSP/SPY +1.9% in a day and +3.8% on the month with acceleration z=3.01, equal-weight S&P at the 91st percentile, Dow flat while NDX fell 2.9%.

Asia stabilized overnight — Hang Seng +0.7%, Shanghai +0.9%, KOSPI +0.3% — with USDCNY at 6.6596 (0th percentile, i.e. strongest yuan of the year) and KRW -1.9% on the month. No EM funding squeeze in Asia.
The defensive engine is working, not just hiding: XLV and XLP both at the 100th percentile, UNH +14.0% and LLY +11.7% on the month, COST +13.2%, WMT +10.0%.
Front-end relief is real: 2y 4.65% (-16bp), 5y 4.78% (-17bp), 10y back under 5% at 4.96%, TLT +1.9%, and 10y real yields -12bp to 2.64%.

bad.text: MOVE 106.84, +11.4% on the day, +36% on the month, z=1.93, acceleration 1.03, 39.7% above its 200-day. Bond vol accelerating while yields fall is a flight, and it is the worst-looking chart on the board.
The whole equity vol curve lifted: VIX +4.0% to 19.79, VIX3M +8.8% on the week, VIX/VIX3M 0.946 at z=1.95 with acceleration 1.30, SKEW 152.39. Hedging is no longer cheap at any tenor.
USDMXN 18.779: z=3.14, 100th percentile, +8.6% on the month, acceleration 1.54 — an accelerating single-country FX accident while EEM/SPY sits at z=-2.39.
Semiconductor de-rating keeps compounding: SOXX -17.0% on the month (acceleration -1.93), MU -21.9%, AMD -18.6%, SMH/SPY z=-2.23, exported to Korea (EWY -22.6%, KOSPI 1m z=-3.0).

Stagflationary twist in breakevens: 5-year 2.45% (+13bp on the month) versus 10-year 2.32% (-1bp), with the 30-year mortgage stuck at 7.32%, 94th percentile. Front-end inflation plus a frozen housing rate is the worst mix for 2027 earnings.

Credit is lagging, not confirming: HYG/IEF -1.9% on the month at z=-1.49 with acceleration -1.06, HYG at the 37th percentile, BKLN z=-1.10. That is how high yield behaves before, not after, it reprices.

trades.name: Software over silicon
trades.line: PAIR long IGV / short SMH - software over AI silicon
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH dollar-neutral, 1:1 notional. Size 3-4% gross per leg.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is being de-rated at the capex/hardware end, not the recurring-revenue end. Semis carry inventory, Korea and Taiwan beta, and China export risk; software carries none of it and is being bought with the proceeds.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +18.2% on the month to z=2.63 with acceleration 2.12 and +38.4% over three months; SOXX -6.8% in a session, -17.0% on the month, SMH/SPY z=-2.23, while IGV is -0.1% on the day and +1.8% on the month.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.195, or MU/AMD both up more than 5% in a week on a capex upgrade cycle.

trades.name: Healthcare leadership
trades.line: LONG XLV - 100th pctile, RS +8% on the month, accel 1.63
trades.expr: Buy XLV; barbell the single names with equal-weight LLY and UNH for the high-beta version.
trades.thesis: Healthcare is the only sector combining 52-week-high price, accelerating relative strength and defensive cash flows. In a tape de-rating growth multiples while nominal GDP stays hot, this is where the index-level money relocates.
trades.trigger: XLV +1.3% on the day, +6.7% on the month, relative strength +8.0% (1m) and +8.7% (3m) with acceleration 1.63, pos52 at 1.00; UNH +14.0% and LLY +11.7% on the month.
trades.stop: XLV below 172 (roughly its 200-day plus the extension it carries), or monthly relative strength vs SPX turning negative.

trades.name: Brazil over Mexico
trades.line: PAIR long EWZ / short EWW - real firm, peso z=3.1 blowout
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, equal dollar. FX purists: long BRL / short MXN spot at 1:1 notional.
trades.thesis: Latin America has split cleanly. Brazil has a firming currency, the best equity trend on the global board, and a commodity mix levered to crude over $100. Mexico has an accelerating currency crisis that its local index is masking.
trades.trigger: USDMXN 18.779, z=3.14 at the 100th percentile, +8.6% on the month with acceleration 1.54, while USDBRL is 5.0351, -1.3% on the month; EWZ +9.4% on the month and 13.3% above its 200-day versus EWW -0.8% on the day and flat on the month.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 18.00, or EWZ closing below its 200-day.
trades.target: 10 points of spread; EWZ 46 with EWW toward 70.

trades.name: Fade the homebuilder squeeze
trades.line: SHORT ITB - fade the squeeze against a 7.32% mortgage
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Dec ITB 88 puts. DHI is the cleanest single-name short expression.
trades.thesis: Builders ripped on a one-day belly rally, but nothing in mortgage finance changed. A 17bp move in the 5-year does not fix a 7.32% primary rate, and the move came with bond vol exploding, which widens, not narrows, mortgage spreads.
trades.trigger: ITB +5.4% and XHB +3.8% in a session, DHI +6.2%, XHB/SPY acceleration z=1.01 — yet ITB is still -0.2% on the month, 4.6% below its 200-day at the 27th percentile, while the 30-year mortgage is 7.32%, +37bp on the month, 94th percentile, and MOVE is at z=1.93.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage prints below 7.00%, or ITB closes above its 200-day near 95.6.

trades.name: 2s30s bull steepener
trades.line: PAIR steepener: long TU vs short UB, DV01-neutral
trades.expr: Long 2-year futures (TU) versus short Ultra Bond (UB), DV01-matched. Options version: 2y receiver vs 30y payer.
trades.thesis: The front end rallies on the growth scare; the long end cannot, because near-term inflation is rising and term premium is being repriced by bond volatility. That is a steepener in both a flight and a cut.
trades.trigger: 2y -16bp to 4.65% versus 30y -13bp to 5.29%; MOVE at z=1.93 and +36% on the month; 5-year breakevens +13bp on the month to 2.45% while 10-year breakevens fell 1bp to 2.32%; 2s10s +6bp on the month at 31bp with acceleration z=1.31.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 20bp, or the 2-year yield back above 4.85% on hawkish repricing.

trades.name: Energy equity over industrials
trades.line: LONG XLE vs SHORT XLI - $101 crude, RS +10.7% on month
trades.expr: Long XLE (or XOM/CVX 50/50), short XLI against it for the beta-neutral version; XOP for the higher-torque leg.
trades.thesis: Crude is above $100 with the Brent risk premium only partially drained, and energy equities are the one cyclical complex at 52-week highs with accelerating relative strength. Industrials carry the capex-cycle and transport weakness that is deteriorating in the same data.
trades.trigger: WTI +1.8% to 101.27, +9.9% on the month, DBC at the 99th percentile; XLE relative strength +10.7% (1m) and +10.3% (3m) with acceleration 1.04, pos52 0.97; XOM +12.3% and CVX +12.0% on the month at the 99th percentile; XLI rolling over with 3-month relative strength -11.4% and CAT -12.9% on the month.
trades.stop: WTI below 94 (the geopolitical premium fully unwinding), or XLE closing below 63.

trades.name: High yield catches down
trades.line: SHORT HYG via puts - junk lagging Treasuries, HYG/IEF z=-1.5
trades.expr: Buy Dec HYG 76 puts, or short HYG against long IEF 1:1 for the carry-neutral version.
trades.thesis: Credit always lags a growth scare. Spreads have not broken, but junk is losing to duration every day, which is the precursor, and the cheapest tail hedge left now that both ends of the VIX curve have repriced.
trades.trigger: HYG/IEF -1.9% on the month to z=-1.49 with acceleration -1.06, HYG at the 37th percentile of its year, BKLN z=-1.10 and -0.8% on the month, against MOVE at z=1.93 and VIX 19.79 and rising.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF reclaims its one-month high, or VIX closes below 16.
